name: Cryogenic carbon capture (desublimation)

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is dried and cooled to about -117 °C or colder so that CO2 freezes out (desublimes) and is separated as a solid, then melted and pumped as high-purity liquid CO2. Cold is recovered between the incoming and outgoing streams in multi-stream heat exchangers.

process_steps.name: CO2 desublimation at about -117 °C
equipment: desublimating heat exchanger or contact liquid vessel

reference_plants.name: Sugar Creek cement plant pilot
reference_plants.status: DOE project Feb 2022 to Apr 2025; target 95% capture and 95% purity

source.note: NETL 2022 Carbon Management meeting, SES presentation

costs.metric: cost of CO2 captured, InnoSepra sorbent-and-membrane cryogenic process, post-combustion power
costs.basis: NETL Compendium status: completed project achieved 'a CO2 capture cost of less than $40/tonne', recorded here as <=40 USD/t; project goal was 'about $30/MT by 2030' with capture cost 'greater than 40% lower' than solvent-based capture; bench-scale TEA, >=90% removal and >95% purity target; dollar year not stated, 2024 is the Compendium publication year; note the InnoSepra design is a sorbent/membrane process operating at near-cryogenic conditions, not the SES desublimation CCC design

source.note: NETL, Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, InnoSepra LLC - Sorbent and Membrane-Cryogenic Carbon Capture, pp. 290-291

advantages: Produces liquid CO2 directly, convenient for shipping
Can also remove other pollutants as they freeze out
limitations: Heavy refrigeration duty; economics depend on cold recovery
